# Testing and Debugging

## Concepts

Verification begins with requirements, not stimulus. Turn each requirement into scenarios, properties, and evidence. Simulation evaluates concrete traces; formal analysis checks behavior under explicit assumptions and either a finite bound or a proof procedure.

A self-checking environment separates the driver, monitor, reference model, and scoreboard. Waveforms help explain a failure, but automated checks decide whether the test passes. Safety properties exclude bad behavior; progress properties require eventual completion and usually need assumptions about the environment.

## Implementation

For a ready/valid FIFO, track reset emptiness, capacity, ordering, and stability during stalls. A reference queue enqueues on accepted inputs and dequeues on accepted outputs. Check both events at the same sampling edge, using the values that determine those transfers.

An output-stability assertion can express a local guarantee:

```systemverilog
assert property (
  @(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
    out_valid && !out_ready |=> out_valid && $stable(out_data)
);
```

The corresponding input property constrains the producer. Assert it when checking an integrated producer; assume it when proving the buffer under a legal external environment. Reset history and initial-state assumptions must be explicit.

When a testbench helper samples after a rising edge, review whether checks observe the transaction at the edge or the updated state after it. A consumer can clear valid on the very edge that completes a transfer; checking only the updated valid can miss that transfer.

## Hands-on Experiments

Create a verification matrix:

| Requirement | Scenario or property | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty after reset | Reset with and without pending data | Automatic check |
| Ordered output | Numbered payload sequence | Queue scoreboard |
| Stable stalled output | Consumer stalls for several cycles | Assertion |
| Capacity respected | Input attempts while full | Occupancy check |
| Sustained throughput | Producer and consumer continuously active | Transfer counts |

Use deterministic seeds and a simulation timeout. Add a deliberate ordering or overwrite fault and ensure the checks detect it. Run a bounded formal case, recording assumptions, depth, engine, and result; a bounded pass alone does not establish unrestricted correctness.
